turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Next patient is Nicole Miller. Date of birth is 09/18/1949. Patient was called for a follow-up with me for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction. She reported being interested in having her right knee replaced this summer at east metro. It was recommended that we work to control her cardiovascular status before surgery. Hey, miss Miller, how are you today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm doing okay, thank you.

turns.text: I asked you to come in today because we want to keep- we want you to have this knee surgery this summer but we want to keep a close eye on you to make sure a week before your surgery you don't suddenly go into congestive heart failure and it gets postponed.

turns.label: Patient

turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Great.

turns.text: Um and after I stopped taking that um I went back to the stomach one, so I'm doing good now.

turns.text: Okay and you're still due for a colonoscopy, correct?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All in all I think you're doing good on paper though.

turns.text: What about, um what's it called, a1c? Does that show up?

turns.text: All righty.

turns.text: So we often like to keep people with heart problems on magnesium and get their levels up to around the 2-ish range.
